issues.legal_issue: A state may impose non-agricultural assessment on government-owned land leased for a business purpose and recover it from an incorporated lessee that is legally distinct from the government.
material_facts: The land was owned by the Union Government and leased to an incorporated company for establishing and operating an industrial plant.
The company’s shares were wholly owned by the Union Government, but the company was a separate legal entity.

The amended assessment scheme included a qualifying government-land lessee within the definition of owner and applied to government land leased for commercial, industrial or other non-agricultural purposes.
issues.conclusion: For the period governed by the amendments, the company was liable as the lessee to pay non-agricultural assessment on qualifying land. Article 285 did not bar the assessment because the land was owned by the Union Government, not by the company, and the company was legally distinct from its shareholder.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 2(j), 3 and 12 of the Andhra Pradesh Non-Agricultural Lands Assessment Act, as amended, a lessee of government land leased for a commercial, industrial or other non-agricultural purpose could be treated as the owner liable for assessment. Article 285 of the Constitution did not exempt property merely because the shares of the incorporated lessee were wholly held by the Union Government. The Court relied on Western Coalfields Limited v. Special Area Development Authority, Rustom Cavasjee Cooper v. Union of India, and Heavy Engineering Mazdoor Union v. State of Bihar for the distinct legal personality of an incorporated company and the distinction between company property and shareholder property.

rule.if: state_non_agricultural_assessment_proceeding and government_owned_land and land_leased_to_incorporated_company and lease_for_non_agricultural_business and lessee_falls_within_assessment_liability

predicates.state_non_agricultural_assessment_procee: A state authority seeks non-agricultural assessment in a proceeding concerning land.
predicates.government_owned_land: The land is owned by a government.
predicates.land_leased_to_incorporated_company: A government leases the land to a company incorporated as a legal entity distinct from its shareholders.
predicates.lease_for_non_agricultural_business: The land is leased for a commercial, industrial or other non-agricultural purpose.
predicates.lessee_falls_within_assessment_liability: The applicable assessment scheme treats a lessee in these circumstances as liable to pay the assessment.

issues.definition: When a state assessment proceeding concerns government-owned land leased to a separate incorporated company for a non-agricultural business and the lessee falls within the assessment liability, the company is liable for the assessment.

issues.legal_issue: Promissory estoppel does not prevent a statutory assessment where the law imposes the assessment, and an assurance limited to government-run units does not exempt a separate incorporated company.
material_facts: A central government letter stated that no separate exemption notification was required while the units were run by the Government of India in the public sector.
The company relied on that correspondence to claim that the State Government was estopped from levying assessment.
The company was a separate legal entity that ran its own industry, and the applicable amended law imposed assessment liability on qualifying lessees.
issues.conclusion: The State Government was not estopped from levying the assessment. There can be no estoppel against a statute, and the correspondence did not promise an exemption to a separate company merely because its shares were government-owned.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the rule that there can be no estoppel against a statute. It also construed the State Government’s letter according to its terms: it concerned units run by the Government of India in the public sector, whereas the company was a distinct legal entity running its own industry. The assessment liability arose under Sections 2(j), 3 and 12 of the Andhra Pradesh Non-Agricultural Lands Assessment Act, as amended.

predicates.state_non_agricultural_assessment_procee: A state authority seeks non-agricultural assessment in a proceeding concerning land.
predicates.statutory_assessment_duty_applies: The applicable law imposes assessment liability on the claimant in the circumstances.
predicates.claimant_invokes_government_assurance: The claimant relies on a government assurance as a reason to resist the assessment.

issues.definition: When a claimant invokes a government assurance in a state assessment proceeding but the applicable law imposes the assessment duty, the assurance does not bar the assessment by promissory estoppel.

issues.legal_issue: An amendment creating assessment liability does not authorize demands for periods before the amendment took effect when the amendment is not retrospective.
material_facts: The demands included periods both before and after the amendments that brought qualifying leased government land within the assessment scheme.
The amendments had no retrospective effect, and the State’s defence to the challenge relied on those amendments.
issues.conclusion: Demands for periods before the amendments took effect were quashed; the amendments did not authorize retrospective assessment.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the amendments to Sections 2(j) and 12 of the Andhra Pradesh Non-Agricultural Lands Assessment Act had no retrospective effect. Therefore, they could not support demands for assessment for periods before they came into force.

predicates.state_non_agricultural_assessment_procee: A state authority seeks non-agricultural assessment in a proceeding concerning land.
predicates.demand_covers_pre_amendment_period: The demand seeks assessment for a period before the relevant amendment took effect.
predicates.liability_depends_on_nonretrospective_am: The asserted liability arises from an amendment that does not apply retrospectively.

issues.definition: When a state assessment demand covers a period before a non-retrospective amendment creating the asserted liability took effect, that demand is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: Assessment on leased government land may be imposed only on the portion actually used for a commercial, industrial or other non-agricultural purpose.
material_facts: The leased area included land covered by buildings and roads, land said to be reserved for future expansion, and land said to be used for agriculture.
The extent actually used for qualifying purposes and the applicable rate had not been determined by the assessing authority.
The company was permitted to pursue those matters in an appeal under the assessment scheme.
issues.conclusion: Only land actually used for a commercial, industrial or other non-agricultural purpose could be assessed. The companies could establish the actual extent of qualifying land and contest the applicable rate in statutory appeals.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 3 and 12 of the Andhra Pradesh Non-Agricultural Lands Assessment Act, as amended, assessment could be levied only on government land leased for a qualifying purpose and actually used for a commercial, industrial or other non-agricultural purpose. The extent of such land and the appropriate rate were matters for determination in the statutory appeal.

predicates.state_non_agricultural_assessment_procee: A state authority seeks non-agricultural assessment in a proceeding concerning land.
predicates.government_land_leased_for_qualifying_pu: Government-owned land is leased for a commercial, industrial or other non-agricultural purpose.
predicates.land_extent_includes_nonqualifying_or_un: The leased area includes portions not actually used for a commercial, industrial or other non-agricultural purpose.

issues.definition: When a state assessment proceeding concerns qualifying leased government land that includes unused or otherwise nonqualifying portions, assessment is limited to the land actually used for a non-agricultural purpose.
